speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with progressive difficulty walking, urinary incontinence, and speech difficulties. To understand the underlying cause, have you noticed if these symptoms worsened quickly over days or gradually over months?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing a gradual difficulty in walking over the past 3 months, requiring wheelchair assistance for the last month. Additionally, there is a history of urinary incontinence for 1 year and recent onset of speech slurring making communication challenging.

speaker: Doctor
text: That progression from incontinence to gait failure and then speech issues is concerning. To narrow down the specific neurological tract involved, have you noticed any significant weakness in your arms or legs, or changes in your sensation like numbness or tingling?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive difficulty walking. I also have Urinary incontinence, Slurred speech, Rigidity in limbs, Mild hand tremor, Orthostatic hypotension.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Multiple System Atrophy (MSA-C). The combination of early autonomic failure (orthostatic hypotension, urinary incontinence), parkinsonian features (rigidity, tremor), and cerebellar signs (gait ataxia, speech slurring) with a progressive course is highly characteristic of this condition.
